targets.title: Brand Experience: What Is It? How Is It Measured? Does It Affect Loyalty?
targets.evidence_quote: In this study we replicate the extended BXS [19] cross-nationally to measure differences in the ways consumers experience the eco-friendliness of global smartphone brands in a cross-national context. The survey items were selected from the previously developed and extended BXS [18,19,107]. We assess the four items measuring eco-friendliness as well as the other four brand experience dimensions from the BXS by conducting structural equation modeling (SEM) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) following the same steps that Brakus et al. targets.outcome_quote: However, based on our study the dimensions for eco-friendly, sensory, affective, and behavioral brand experiences are generalizable cross-nationally in India and Finland. Even so, our findings suggest that the intellectual aspects of the brand experience should be localized with special expertise of the consumer groups in the target country.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original four-factor structure is empirically retested, with sensory, affective and behavioral dimensions supported but intellectual dimension not confirmed in India. Statements validating a revised model do not constitute an overall verdict confirming the original structure.

targets.outcome_quote: The findings of our study indicate that the eco-friendliness dimension can be generalized in two countries with very different demographics and economic situations.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The earlier eco-friendliness dimension is explicitly retested and confirmed in both countries; changes to the other dimensions do not negate this target finding.
